subject: Evaluation roadmap + stakeholder roles for PulseHealth POC
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Rivera <anna@pulsehealth.com>, Tom Whitaker <tom.whitaker@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Evaluation roadmap + stakeholder roles for PulseHealth POC

Anna / Tom —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I wanted to share a concise kickoff note to align on scope, success criteria, owners, and the benchmark plan for the 6-week POC. Attached is a one-page MAP workbook (redwood_map_v1.xlsx) and a short benchmark spec (pulse_benchmark_spec.md) so everyone has the same frame.

High-level goal: demonstrate a reproducible pipeline for clinical note summarization that meets PulseHealth latency and quality targets while showing unit-cost improvements vs your current solution. Proposed acceptance gates below.

Key success criteria (proposed)
- Precision target: ROUGE-L F1 >= 0.68 on the dev benchmark set
- Latency: 95th percentile generation <= 450ms for 512-token budget on r4 GPUs
- Cost: inference unit cost <= $0.0017/token at steady-state (projected with caching + batching)
- Integration: 2-way API + auth test with your staging environment by week 3

Suggested owners (Redwood / PulseHealth)
- MAP owner (overall) — Mina Haddad (Redwood) / Anna Rivera (PulseHealth)
- Bench & eval owner — Ben Carter (Redwood) / Tom Whitaker (PulseHealth)
- Prompt / dataset steward — PulseHealth data team (TBD), review with Marissa Cole (CS)
- Security & compliance checklist — PulseHealth security + Redwood trust team (we'll loop them in)

Immediate asks
1) Can you confirm the dev benchmark dataset location and a point-of-contact for dataset access?
2) Please review the attached success criteria and flag any thresholds that need changing by EOD Friday (7/3).
3) Do the names above for owners make sense, or should we reassign?

Proposed next steps
- Wed 7/1 10:00am PT: 30m alignment call to finalize owners and data handoff (invite sent)
- Week 1: Dataset access + baseline run (Redwood provides reference pipeline)
- Week 2–3: Bench runs + prompt iteration; week 3: staging API test
- Week 5–6: Optimization and final acceptance run

Attachments: redwood_map_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), pulse_benchmark_spec.md (bench plan)

Looking forward — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Mina — this is great and aligns with our internal priorities. A few quick notes from our side: 

1) Dataset access / contacts
- Primary: Tom Whitaker (cc'd) will own the dataset delivery (staging S3) and will create a sanitized dev snapshot by tomorrow EOD.
- Secondary: I'll assign our clinical SME, Priya Das, to the prompt review cadence.

2) Success criteria adjustments
- ROUGE-L target: we prefer 0.70 as an initial bar; if needed we can tier acceptance (0.70 gold / 0.66 silver) so we have a path to close.
- Latency: 95th <= 500ms is acceptable given our downstream processing; 450ms would be lovely but not blocking.

3) Security checklist
- We'll need an inventory of logs that Redwood collects during the POC and retention windows — can your trust team outline that before week 2?

Availability: Wed 7/1 10am PT works for me (I accepted the invite).

Attachments: none

Anna / team —

Quick follow-up on the benchmark plan and execution owners from Redwood's side. I've sketched a sprint-aligned bench schedule in the attached spec, but highlighting the owners here: 

- Bench setup & baseline run: Ben Carter (AE) + infra team (ops) — week 1
- Prompt iteration and eval harness: Mina Haddad (SSE) + Marissa Cole (CS) — week 2–3
- Cost modeling & quantization experiments: Redwood research (lead: A. Liu) — week 3–5
- Integration / staging API tests: Marissa Cole (CS) + Tom Whitaker (PulseHealth) — week 3

I've also included a minimal runbook in pulse_benchmark_spec.md that lists the exact endpoints we'll hit, sample prompt templates, metric collection schema (ROUGE / BLEU / toxicity cursory checks), and a table of test vectors your SME should validate.

One operational note: to meet the 95th latency target consistently we'll enable prefix caching for the clinical note prefixes you mentioned. That will be an opt-in toggle in the staging API and requires a short data contract (we only store hashed prefixes in memory; no PII persisted). I'll coordinate the trust checklist with our security contact.

If the team is comfortable, I propose we finalize the MAP workbook during the 7/1 call and convert to a shared Drive doc for live edits.

Ben
